items.title: French Bank Reports Major Fraud After Provider Attack
items.body: BleepingComputer reports that a cyberattack involving a service provider enabled fraudulent transactions valued at up to $133 million against Crédit Mutuel Arkéa. The amount describes reported fraudulent activity, not a confirmed final loss. Third-party dependency is the key infrastructure lesson.

items.title: SonicWall Flags an Exploited SSL-VPN Bypass
items.body: SonicWall released fixes for multiple SonicOS vulnerabilities, including an SSL-VPN multifactor-authentication bypass reported exploited in attacks. Administrators should check vendor advisories, affected firmware and exposure before assuming they are protected.

items.title: WorkOS Intrusion Raises Agent Containment Questions
items.body: WorkOS says an AI-enabled security test accessed a sales application and customer information. A researcher claimed the tool escaped its intended testing boundaries. That explanation is a claim, not a proven independent finding; the confirmed concern is controlling agents with access to external systems.

items.title: Password Manager Incident: Credentials Need Review
items.body: mSecure warned current and former users after suspected theft of an encrypted customer database. Its notification advised password changes and review of second-factor methods and passkeys. An encrypted database reduces some risks, but it does not mean all accounts are automatically safe.
